questions.question: Superconductors are derived from the compounds of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transition elements.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Superconductors:**

 
• Superconductivity is a set of physical properties:
 
 
• **electrical resistance vanishes **
 
• **magnetic flux fields are expelled from the material.**
 
 
 
• Unlike an ordinary metallic conductor, whose** resistance decreases gradually as its temperature** is **lowered **even down to near absolute zero
 
• A superconductor has a **characteristic critical temperature below which the resistance drops abruptly to zero.**
 
• An electric current through a** loop of superconducting wire can persist indefinitely with no power source.**
 
• Superconductor material classes include chemical element**s (e.g. mercury or lead), alloys (such as niobium-titanium, germanium–niobium, and niobium nitride), ceramics (YBCO and magnesium diboride)**, etc.
 
• Superconductors are **mostly compounds of transition metal. *Hence option 4 is correct.***

questions.question: Which of the following element has maximum density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Osmium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Osmium is a dense metal belonging to the platinum group and has the highest density of any naturally occurring element.
 
• Its density is approximately 22.59 grams per cubic centimeter, making it the densest natural element.
 
• Osmium is used in alloys with other platinum-group metals to produce extremely hard materials for specialized applications.
 
• It is a hard, brittle metal with a bluish tint and is typically found in nature as an alloy with other platinum group metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Density:** Density is defined as the mass per unit volume of a substance. It is typically expressed in grams per cubic centimeter (g/cm³). The formula for density is:

 
 
• Density = Mass / Volume
 
 
 
• **Platinum Group Metals (PGM):** These are six metallic elements clustered together in the periodic table. They are platinum (Pt), palladium (Pd), rhodium (Rh), ruthenium (Ru), iridium (Ir), and osmium (Os). These metals have similar physical and chemical properties and tend to occur together in the same mineral deposits.
 
• **Applications of Osmium:**
 
 
• Osmium is used in fountain pen tips, electrical contacts, and in other applications where extreme durability and hardness are needed.
 
• Osmium tetroxide, a compound of osmium, is used in staining tissues in electron microscopy.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Elements:**
 
 
• Lead has a density of approximately 11.34 g/cm³, which is significantly lower than osmium.
 
• Platinum has a density of around 21.45 g/cm³, which is also lower than osmium but still very high.
 
• Mercury has a density of approximately 13.53 g/cm³.

questions.question:
A student took iron nails and dipped them in solution 'X' for twenty minutes. After some time he noticed that the colour of the iron nails became brownish.

Identify solution 'X' in which the nail was dipped.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When iron nails are dipped in a solution of copper sulphate, a chemical reaction takes place where iron displaces copper from the solution.
 
• The reaction is a type of single displacement reaction where iron (Fe) reacts with copper sulphate (CuSO₄) to form iron sulphate (FeSO₄) and copper (Cu).
 
• The brownish colour observed on the iron nails is due to the deposition of copper metal on the surface of the iron nails.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.
 
• This reaction indicates that iron is more reactive than copper, as it displaces copper from its compound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Single Displacement Reaction:**

 
 
• A chemical reaction where one element displaces another element from its compound.
 
• It usually occurs between a more reactive metal and a less reactive metal compound.
 
• Example: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity Series of Metals:**
 
 
• A list of metals arranged in order of their reactivity, from most reactive to least reactive.
 
• Iron is more reactive than copper, which is why it can displace copper from copper sulphate solution.
 
 
 
• **Copper Sulphate (CuSO₄):**
 
 
• A blue crystalline solid used in various chemical reactions and applications.
 
• Commonly used in laboratories and for agricultural purposes.
 
 
 
• **Iron (Fe):**
 
 
• A common metal known for its strength and magnetic properties.
 
• Widely used in construction, manufacturing, and various industrial applications.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most reactive metal in the reactivity series?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Potassium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium** is known to be the most reactive metal in the reactivity series.
 
• It belongs to the **alkali metals group** in the periodic table, which is Group 1.
 
• Potassium reacts **vigorously with water**, producing hydrogen gas and heat, which can ignite the hydrogen.
 
• Its high reactivity is due to its **single valence electron**, which it can easily lose to form a positive ion.
 
• This metal must be stored in **oil or an inert atmosphere** to prevent it from reacting with moisture or oxygen in the air.
 
• Potassium is used in various applications, including **fertilizers** and as a critical element in biological processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gold**__

 __
 
• **Gold** is a less reactive metal and is found in its native form in nature.
 
• It is highly valued for its **non-reactivity** and is used extensively in **jewelry** and **electronics** due to its excellent **conductivity**.
 
 
 
• **Zinc**__
 __
 
• **Zinc** is a moderately reactive metal.
 
• It is commonly used for **galvanization** to protect iron and steel from corrosion.
 
 
 
• **Sodium**__
 
 
• **Sodium** is also highly reactive, similar to potassium, and is part of the **alkali metals group**.
 
• It reacts vigorously with **water and oxygen** and is used in various **industrial processes**.

questions.question: A metal is extracted from cinnabar ore by strong heating. What are alloys of this metal with other metals collectively known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amalgam**.__

__**Concept:**__

**Alloy:** An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a non-metal. 

**Mineral: **Minerals are **naturally occurring inorganic solids** with a crystalline structure and a definite range of chemical formulas.

**Ore: **Ores are **concentrations of minerals** in rock that are high enough to be **economically extracted for use.**

**__Explanation:__**

**Cinnabar:**

__
 
• It is bright red or brownish-red mineral formed of **mercuric sulfide **(mercury(II) sulfide).
 
• It is found close to areas of volcanic activity and hot springs.
 
• It is the **main commercial source of mercury**.
 
• **Chemical Formula: HgS.**

**Amalgam**

 
• It is an **alloy of mercury **and one or more other metals.
 
• It is **crystalline in structure,** except for those with a high mercury content, which is liquid.

So, **the metal extracted from cinnabar ore by strong heating is Mercury and the alloys of this metal with other metals are collectively known as amalgam.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Nichrome**: It is an alloy of nickel, chromium, and iron** (Ni + Cr + Fe).**
 
• **Steel: ** It is an alloy of iron and carbon **(****Fe + C).**
 
• **German silver:** It is an alloy of** **copper, zinc, and nickel (**Cu + Zn + Ni).**

questions.question: Which of the following elements is more reactive than copper?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zinc (Zn)**

 
 
• Reactivity: Zinc is a moderately reactive metal.
 
• Reacts with acids (like hydrochloric acid) to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• Reacts with strong bases (like sodium hydroxide) to form complex ions.
 
• Reacts with oxygen in the air to form zinc oxide.
 
• Can displace less reactive metals (like copper) from their salt solutions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Platinum (Pt)**

 
 
• Reactivity: Platinum is a noble metal, meaning it is very resistant to corrosion and chemical reactions.
 
• Reactions:
 
• Does not readily react with most acids, including hydrochloric acid and sulfuric acid.
 
• Reacts with aqua regia (a mixture of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid).
 
• Can form compounds with a few highly reactive elements like fluorine and chlorine.
 
 
 
• **Silver (Ag)**
 
 
• Reactivity: Silver is less reactive than zinc but more reactive than platinum and gold.
 
• Reactions:
 
• Reacts with sulfur and its compounds to form silver sulfide (tarnish).
 
• Reacts with nitric acid and concentrated sulfuric acid.
 
• Can be oxidized by ozone.
 
 
 
• **Gold (Au)**
 
 
• Reactivity: Gold is one of the least reactive metals.
 
• Reactions:
 
• Does not react with most acids, including hydrochloric acid and sulfuric acid.
 
• Reacts with aqua regia.
 
• Can form compounds with a few highly reactive elements like fluorine and chlorine.

questions.question: Although metals form basic oxides, which of the following metals form an amphoteric oxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Al**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aluminum (Al)** forms an amphoteric oxide, which means it can react with both acids and bases to form salts and water.
 
• Amphoteric oxides are a characteristic of some metals, and they are unique because they exhibit both basic and acidic properties.
 
• Other metals in the options provided, such as sodium (Na), copper (Cu), and calcium (Ca), form oxides that are predominantly basic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Amphoteric behavior is due to the metal having an intermediate electronegativity and the ability to form stable bonds with both hydrogen and hydroxide ions.
 
• Examples of amphoteric oxides include aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) and zinc oxide (ZnO).
 
• Aluminum oxide reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl) to form aluminum chloride (AlCl₃) and water, and with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to form sodium aluminate (NaAlO₂) and water.

questions.question: Which of the following metals CANNOT be cut with a knife?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium, lithium, and potassium are alkali metals that are soft and can be cut with a knife.
 
• Alkali metals are known for their softness and low density.
 
• Copper is a transition metal, which is much harder and cannot be cut with a knife.
 
• The hardness of a metal is determined by its atomic structure and bonding.
 
• Alkali metals have a single electron in their outer shell, which makes them highly reactive and soft.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkali Metals**

 
 
• These metals are found in Group 1 of the periodic table.
 
• They are highly reactive, especially with water, and are stored in oil to prevent reactions with moisture in the air.
 
• Examples include lithium, sodium, and potassium.
 
 
 
• **Transition Metals**
 
 
• These metals are found in the central block of the periodic table (Groups 3-12).
 
• They are characterized by their ability to form variable oxidation states and colored compounds.
 
• Examples include copper, iron, and gold.
 
 
 
• **Metals and Their Properties**
 
 
• Metals are generally malleable, ductile, and good conductors of electricity and heat.
 
• The physical properties of metals vary widely across the periodic table.
 
• Reactivity, hardness, and melting points of metals can differ significantly based on their atomic structure and bonding.

questions.question: Which of the following metals **does not** react with dilute Hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The **metal reactivity series governs metal reactivity.**
 
• **Metals placed above hydrogen react with dilute acids** to form salt, whereas **metals placed below hydrogen do not react with dilute acids** because they are** less reactive than hydrogen** and thus cannot displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
 
• Copper **metal does not** react **with dilute Hydrochloric acid** __because it is placed below hydrogen in the metal reactivity series, and thus it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****Iron**

 
• Iron metals do indeed** react with dilute hydrochloric acid.**
 
• The reaction between iron and hydrochloric acid is a classic example of a **metal-acid reaction**.

Fe (s) + 2HCl (aq) → FeCl₂ (aq) + H₂ (g)

Magnesium

 
• When magnesium is treated with dilute hydrochloric acid, it forms magnesium chloride and emits hydrogen gas.

Mg (s) + 2HCl (aq) → MgCl2 (aq) + H2(g)

**Aluminum**

 
• At room temperature, aluminum reacts with diluted hydrochloric acid. 
 
• Aluminum chloride and colourless hydrogen gas are produced when the metal aluminum dissolves in hydrochloric acid.
 
• The reaction between aluminum and hydrochloric acid is irreversible.

2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl3 + 3H2

questions.question: On oxidation, silver changes its colour to _______ and copper changes its colour to _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**black; green**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On oxidation, **silver turns black** due to the formation of silver sulfide (Ag2S).
 
• Silver sulfide forms when silver reacts with hydrogen sulfide in the air.
 
• **Copper turns green** upon oxidation due to the formation of copper carbonate (CuCO3).
 
• This green layer on copper is commonly known as patina.
 
• Patina forms when copper reacts with carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O) in the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:**

 
 
• Oxidation is a chemical reaction in which a material loses electrons, often resulting in a change in color.
 
• It commonly occurs when metals react with oxygen or other oxidizing agents.
 
 
 
• **Silver Sulfide (Ag2S):**
 
 
• It is a black compound formed when silver reacts with sulfur or hydrogen sulfide.
 
• Ag2S is responsible for the tarnishing of silver objects.
 
 
 
• **Copper Carbonate (CuCO3):**
 
 
• It forms a green layer known as patina on the surface of copper.
 
• This green patina acts as a protective layer against further corrosion.
 
 
 
• **Patina:**
 
 
• Patina is the green or brown film on the surface of metals like copper and bronze, produced by oxidation over a long period.
 
• It is often valued aesthetically and can act as a protective layer.

questions.question: The non-metal which exists in a liquid state at room temperature 25 degrees Celcius is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bromine** is the only non-metal that exists in a liquid state at **room temperature (25°C)**. Most non-metals are gases at room temperature, but bromine is an exception.
 
• **Physical state:** Bromine is a reddish-brown liquid with a strong and unpleasant odor. It remains in liquid form due to its relatively higher intermolecular forces compared to other non-metals.
 
• The **melting point of bromine** is about **-7.2°C**, and its **boiling point** is around **59°C**. This temperature range allows bromine to exist as a liquid at room temperature.
 
• Bromine is found naturally in compounds such as bromides in sea water and salt lakes. It is extracted through chemical processes involving chlorine and brine solutions.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Bromine.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Bromine:**

 
 
• **Appearance:** Bromine is a reddish-brown liquid at room temperature, making it visually distinct from other elements.
 
• **Density:** Bromine has a density of about **3.1 g/cm³**, which is higher than water.
 
• **Reactivity:** Bromine is highly reactive and forms compounds with many elements, including metals and non-metals.
 
• **Uses:** Bromine is used in the production of flame retardants, water treatment chemicals, and certain pharmaceuticals.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Argon:** Argon is a noble gas and exists in a gaseous state at room temperature. It is inert and does not chemically react under normal conditions.
 
• **Iodine:** Iodine is a solid at room temperature. It sublimates directly into gas without becoming a liquid under normal conditions.
 
• **Mercury:** Mercury is a metal, not a non-metal, and it exists as a liquid at room temperature. However, the question specifically asks for a non-metal.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• **Temperature Effects:** The physical state of elements depends on their melting and boiling points relative to room temperature.
 
• **Chemical Properties:** Non-metals typically form covalent bonds and have low density compared to metals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Differences Between Metals and Non-Metals:**

 
 
• **Metals:** Typically solid at room temperature (except mercury), good conductors of heat and electricity, malleable, and ductile.
 
• **Non-Metals:** Exist in various states (solid, liquid, or gas), are poor conductors of heat and electricity, brittle in solid form.
 
 
 
• **Unique Properties of Bromine:** Bromine’s liquid state at room temperature distinguishes it from most other non-metals, making it significant for scientific and industrial applications.

questions.question:
How many of the following pairs are incorrect?

1. German Silver: Cu, Zn, Ni

2. Gun Metal: Cu, Zn, Fe

3. Solder: Sn, Pb

4. Duralium: Al, Cu, Mg, Mn

5. Stainless steel: Fe, Cu, Cr, Ni
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **German Silver** is composed of **Copper (Cu), Zinc (Zn), and Nickel (Ni)**. This is correct as it is widely used in decorative items and electrical components.
 
• **Gun Metal** is incorrectly listed as composed of **Copper (Cu), Zinc (Zn), and Iron (Fe)**. The correct composition is **Copper (Cu), Tin (Sn), and Zinc (Zn)**, commonly used for casting and bearings.
 
• **Solder** is correctly composed of **Tin (Sn) and Lead (Pb)**. It is used in electronics and plumbing for joining metals.
 
• **Duralium (Duralumin)** is correctly composed of **Aluminum (Al), Copper (Cu), Magnesium (Mg), and Manganese (Mn)**. It is lightweight and used in aircraft construction.
 
• **Stainless Steel** is incorrectly listed as composed of **Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu), Chromium (Cr), and Nickel (Ni)**. The correct composition includes **Iron (Fe), Chromium (Cr), Nickel (Ni), and often small amounts of Carbon (C) and Molybdenum (Mo)**, used for its corrosion resistance.
 
• Thus, **two pairs are incorrect**: Gun Metal and Stainless Steel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **German Silver:** Despite the name, it contains no silver. It is widely used for items like musical instruments and jewelry due to its resemblance to silver.
 
• **Gun Metal:** It is a type of bronze alloy with high resistance to corrosion and wear, making it suitable for marine applications and engineering components.
 
• **Solder:** Lead-based solder is commonly used in electronics; however, lead-free alternatives are becoming popular due to environmental concerns.
 
• **Duralium:** Its high strength-to-weight ratio makes it ideal for aerospace applications, particularly in the construction of aircraft frames and structures.
 
• **Stainless Steel:** The chromium content (typically 10.5% or higher) gives stainless steel its corrosion resistance. It is widely used in kitchen utensils, medical equipment, and construction.

questions.question: Based on the reactivity series of metals, which of the following metals are most likely to be found in the free state (native state) in nature?
questions.solution:
Answer: __**Cu, Ag, Au.​**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Reactivity Series and Metal Extraction:**

 
 
• 
 
Metals at the bottom of the activity series are the least reactive.

 
 
• 
 
These metals are often found in the free state, such as gold, silver, platinum, and copper.

 
 
• 
 
Copper and silver are also found in combined states as their sulphide or oxide ores.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Highly Reactive Metals:**

 
 
• 
 
Metals at the top of the activity series (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) are very reactive.

 
 
• 
 
These metals are never found in nature as free elements.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Moderately Reactive Metals:**

 
 
• 
 
Metals in the middle of the activity series (Zn, Fe, Pb) are moderately reactive.

 
 
• 
 
These metals are found in the earth’s crust mainly as oxides, sulphides, or carbonates.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Ores and Oxides:**

 
 
• 
 
Many metal ores are oxides because oxygen is a highly reactive and abundant element on Earth.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Categories of Metals Based on Reactivity:**

 
 
• 
 
**Metals of low reactivity**

 
 
• 
 
**Metals of medium reactivity**

 
 
• 
 
**Metals of high reactivity**

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Extraction Techniques:**

 
 
• 
 
Different techniques are used for extracting metals in each category:

 
 
• 
 
**Reduction using carbon**

 
 
• 
 
**Electrolysis**

 
 
• 
 
**Found in native state**

 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Enrichment of Ores:**

 
 
• 
 
Ores mined from the earth often contain impurities like soil, sand, etc., called gangue.

 
 
• 
 
Gangue must be removed before metal extraction.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9dfe41aeec296b9fee0a81ea0c56b65abd69de0c57395ec2abef00c6629056fc.png]

questions.question: The most malleable metal is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gold is the most malleable metal**, meaning it can be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without breaking.
 
• A single gram of gold can be hammered into a sheet of approximately 1 square meter in area.
 
• This exceptional malleability makes gold ideal for crafting fine jewelry, intricate patterns, and thin foils used in various industries.
 
• Gold retains its malleability even when combined with small amounts of other metals, making it versatile for alloy production.
 
• Among all metals, gold also exhibits high ductility, which is the ability to be drawn into thin wires, further emphasizing its unique physical properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malleability:** It is the property of metals that allows them to be deformed under compressive stress, typically by hammering or rolling.
 
• **Ductility:** While gold is the most malleable metal, it is also highly ductile, meaning it can be stretched into thin wires, an essential property for electrical and decorative uses.
 
• **Gold’s Atomic Structure:** Gold has a face-centered cubic (FCC) crystal structure that contributes to its excellent malleability and ductility.
 
• **Industrial Applications:** Besides jewelry, gold's malleable nature is used in electronics, dentistry, and aerospace industries due to its corrosion resistance and conductivity.
 
• **Comparison with Other Metals:** While platinum, silver, and copper also exhibit malleability, they do not surpass gold in their ability to be shaped into ultra-thin sheets.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is placed above aluminium and zinc in the reactivity series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium**__.

**NOTE:** In the official PYP, the question asked about the element placed between Zinc and Aluminium, and the answer was given as **Magnesium**, which is incorrect. We have modified the question to instead ask which element is **more reactive and placed above Aluminium and Zinc**, for which the correct answer is **Magnesium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the **reactivity series**, metals are arranged based on their ability to lose electron

questions.question:
Select the correct statements from the following.

I. All the metals are same in reactivity.

II. Iron can replace copper from copper sulphate solution.

III. Copper can replace iron from ferrous sulphate solution.

IV. Sodium is too soft to cut with a knife.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II and IV**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement II:** Iron can replace copper from copper sulphate solution because iron is more reactive than copper. This is based on the reactivity series of metals.
 
• **Statement IV:** Sodium is a highly reactive alkali metal that is soft and can be easily cut with a knife due to its low density and metallic bonding.
 
• **Statement I is incorrect:** All metals do not have the same reactivity. The reactivity of metals varies and is arranged in the reactivity series.
 
• **Statement III is incorrect:** Copper cannot replace iron from ferrous sulphate solution because copper is less reactive than iron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series:** A list of metals arranged in order of their decreasing reactivity. Highly reactive metals like sodium and potassium are at the top, while less reactive metals like gold and silver are at the bottom.
 
• **Displacement Reaction:** A chemical reaction in which a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound (e.g., iron displaces copper from copper sulphate).
 
• **Properties of Sodium:** Sodium is an alkali metal with low melting point and density. It reacts vigorously with water and oxygen, and it is so soft that it can be cut with a knife.
 
• **Metal Reactivity:** Reactivity of a metal determines its ability to lose electrons and form positive ions. Highly reactive metals like alkali metals react easily, while noble metals like gold and platinum are least reactive.
 
• **Chemical Behavior of Copper:** Copper is a less reactive metal and cannot displace more reactive metals such as iron from their compounds.

questions.question: A metal wire is stretched, but it does not break easily. This property is known as:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**ductility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ductility** refers to the ability of a material to be stretched into a wire without breaking.
 
• This property is commonly associated with metals, allowing them to be drawn into **thin wires**.
 
• **Gold** and **silver** are examples of highly ductile metals.
 
• **Ductility** is a key factor in industrial applications, especially in **electrical wiring** and **metal forming**.
 
• It is measured by the material’s ability to undergo significant **plastic deformation** before rupture.
 
• Materials with high **ductility** can absorb significant stress and strain, making them ideal for construction and manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hardness**__

 __
 
• **Hardness** is the measure of a material's resistance to deformation, particularly indentation or scratching.
 
• It is often assessed using tests like the **Mohs hardness test** or the **Rockwell hardness test**.
 
• Materials like **diamonds** are known for their high hardness.
 
 
 
• **Malleability**__
 __
 
• **Malleability** is the ability of a material to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without breaking.
 
• Examples of malleable materials include **gold** and **aluminum**.
 
• This property is crucial for applications in **metalworking** and **manufacturing**.
 
 
 
• **Brittleness**__
 
 
• **Brittleness** refers to the tendency of a material to break or shatter without significant deformation when under stress.
 
• Brittle materials, like **glass** and **ceramics**, have low ductility and malleability.
